title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §g) of the analysis of the big diagram (62)/(67). It belongs to the study of the 'équation des lacets' for a group 𝔖 (finite or profinite) with two distinguished elements or automorphisms ρ, σ.

On the previous page, Grothendieck has four groups Z_{ρ,σ}, N^+_ρ, N^+_σ and G_{ρ,σ}. Each maps epimorphically onto a common quotient γ_{ρ,σ}. Nine groups are obtained from them by taking fibre products over γ_{ρ,σ} of certain sub-families. The initial term is the fibre product of all four; the terminal term is γ_{ρ,σ} itself.

On this page he passes to the 'special' parts, i.e. the kernels of the maps to γ_{ρ,σ}. These are L_0 = SZ_{ρ,σ}, SN*_ρ, SN*_σ and G^+ = SG_{ρ,σ}.
- Since the kernel of a fibre product over γ of groups over γ is the ordinary product of the kernels, the nine-term diagram becomes one of the same combinatorial type.
- That diagram is made of ordinary partial products of these four groups.
- The arrows are the canonical projections.
- The terminal term is the empty product {1} = Ker(γ_{ρ,σ} →id γ_{ρ,σ}).

He then notes what (62) actually displays: only a few of these product groups (the crossed-out 'cinq' was apparently corrected), each with its canonical injection into the fibre product it comes from. He then lists the further pieces of the diagram:
- the three groups SN*_ρ, SN*_σ and SG_{ρ,σ} = G^+;
- the canonical inclusions SN*_ρ ⊂ N*_ρ, SN*_σ ⊂ N*_σ and G^+ ⊂ G_{ρ,σ};
- the complete diagrams of projections of the partial products of these groups and L_0, including the projections onto the three groups;
- the maps of these groups and of L_0 to the unit group.

The purpose is purely to organise the bookkeeping of the symmetry groups attached to (ρ, σ). This prepares §6°) on the next page, which introduces the set Σ_{ρ,σ} and SG_{ρ,σ} = {(α, β, μ) | [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1^{μ−1}}. That set is a description of the 'special' part of the solution set of the loop equation, à la GT-type relations.
errors: The previous page speaks of taking the 'images' of the nine groups in γ_{ρ,σ', while this page describes the resulting groups as kernels (S-groups, {1} = Ker(id)). 'Kernels' is evidently what is meant; 'images' is a slip or an imprecise wording.
With four factors there are 16 subsets, but only nine groups are listed. This is consistent only if 'certain' sub-families are used, as stated; no actual error.

ideas.what: The kernel of the map from a fibre product of groups over γ to γ is the direct product of the individual kernels. So a diagram of fibre products over γ induces a diagram of the same shape made of ordinary products of the 'special' (kernel) subgroups, with the empty product equal to {1}.
ideas.modern_name: Kernels commute with limits; fibre products over a base restrict to products on fibres
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard category theory / group theory folklore

ideas.what: Organisation of the symmetry groups of the loop equation (Z_{ρ,σ}, N_ρ, N_σ, G_{ρ,σ} and their special parts) into a single cubical-type diagram over the quotient γ_{ρ,σ}.
ideas.modern_name: Bookkeeping of stabiliser/normaliser groups for GT-type ('loop equation') relations in finite quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (unpublished); related to later work on GT actions on dessins and finite quotients (Ihara, Drinfeld, Schneps, Lochak)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely organisational bookkeeping of a diagram of groups: kernels of fibre products become products. It contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The word inserted above 'groupes' in the line 'les projections sur ces ... groupes' reads 'trois'.
The crossed-out word in 'seulement [-...-] parmi ces groupes produits' looks like 'cinq', as transcribed, but is uncertain.
In the line 'les inclusions canoniques ...', the second group is written SN*_σ ↪ N*_σ, and the third is G^+ = SG_{ρ,σ} ↪ G_{ρ,σ}.
The inserted word above 'des projections' reads 'complets'.
